description: API of the HinterOS session daemon, served to the launcher (and other clients running as the session user). Responses to system.*, auth.*, store.list and session.restart may arrive out of order relative to other calls on the same connection (match them by id): a relayed call can wait minutes for an admin password. See hinteros-docs/design/api.md for the protocol rules.

hello.summary: Version handshake. Must be the first request on a connection.
hello.description: The client sends the API version it was built against. Majors must match (during 0.x the minor must match too). The result carries the negotiated version: min(client, server). On a mismatch the server answers with version_mismatch and closes the connection. The client name 'hinteros-osk' is reserved for the on-screen keyboard: such connections receive input_nav while the keyboard is visible, and only then.

ping.summary: Liveness check. Echoes the optional nonce.

subscribe.summary: Start receiving the given events on this connection. Returns the full subscription set.

unsubscribe.summary: Stop receiving the given events. Returns the remaining subscription set.

apps.list.summary: Apps the launcher can show and launch: the built-in 'steam' entry (Steam's Big Picture mode, since 0.3), then the apps from the daemon's config, or a fixed stub list when none are configured.
apps.list.description: Installed Steam games are listed by games.list, not here.

games.list.summary: Installed Steam games of the session user, read from Steam's library on disk.
games.list.description: Read from the Steam directory (~/.local/share/Steam, else ~/.steam/steam; configurable): every library in steamapps/libraryfolders.vdf and its steamapps/appmanifest_<appid>.acf files. Steam tools (Proton, Steam Linux Runtime, Steamworks Common Redistributables, ...) are left out. Empty when Steam is not installed. Sorted by name. Launch a game with apps.launch {url: 'steam://rungameid/<appid>'}. games_changed says when to query again.

steam.attention.summary: Steam's own windows that appeared while something else had focus and still wait to be seen (Steam Guard, update prompts, cloud-save conflicts, sign-in, ...).
steam.attention.description: The same list steam_attention sends. A window stops needing attention when it closes or once Steam has had focus while it was open (steam.focus, apps.launch/apps.focus 'steam'). Always empty without gamescope.

steam.focus.summary: Bring Steam's own windows to the front (e.g. after steam_attention). Controller input goes to Steam.
steam.focus.description: Steam then runs as the app 'steam' (source 'steam_client'; app_started if it was not running) and has focus; its pending windows no longer need attention. When Steam's windows close, focus returns to the app that had it before (or the launcher). Home brings the launcher back as usual.

error.message: Steam has no windows to show

apps.launch.summary: Start an app and give it focus. Returns once it is spawned, before it shows a window.
apps.launch.description: Exactly one of: 'id' (an app from apps.list), 'command' (argv, run as the session user), or 'url' (a Steam game, handed to the running Steam client; use it for games.list entries). If the app is already running it is focused instead and the result describes the running instance. Its windows are shown as soon as they appear; until then the launcher stays visible. Progress is reported through app_started, focus_changed and app_exited. The built-in id 'steam' opens Steam's Big Picture mode (steam://open/bigpicture, or 'steam -gamepadui' when Steam is not running) and shows Steam's own windows; it runs as the app 'steam' with source 'steam_client'. A Steam game's name comes from its Steam library manifest when it is installed.

command.description: Program and arguments. The program is looked up in the daemon's PATH.

url.description: A Steam game, launched through the configured steam binary.

name.description: Display name for a 'command' launch (default: the program's file name).

error.message: cannot start does-not-exist: No such file or directory (os error 2)

apps.running.summary: Apps started through apps.launch that are still running, and which one has focus.
apps.running.description: Re-query this after reconnecting: app_started, app_exited and focus_changed are not replayed.

apps.focus.summary: Bring a running app, or the launcher (null), to the front.
apps.focus.description: Focusing the launcher does not stop the app that had focus. Controller input goes to whatever has focus; while the launcher has focus it arrives as input_nav events.

apps.close.summary: Ask a running app to quit; force it after a timeout. Returns at once, app_exited (reason 'closed') follows.
apps.close.description: A 'command' app gets SIGTERM (through its reaper, to its process group), and after the close timeout (default 5 s) everything still running under its reaper gets SIGKILL. A Steam game: every process under Steam's reaper for that app id gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after the timeout; Steam itself keeps running. A Steam game that has no processes yet (still being prepared by Steam) just stops being tracked. Steam ('steam_client'): Big Picture is asked to close (steam://close/bigpicture); Steam keeps running in the background. Closing an app that is already closing does nothing. If the app had focus, the launcher gets it back when it exits.

osk.show.summary: Show the on-screen keyboard over whatever has focus.
osk.show.description: The on-screen keyboard is a separate client (hinteros-osk) whose window the daemon shows as a gamescope overlay; it never takes focus, so typed keys reach the focused app. While it is visible, InputPlumber is in intercept mode ALL and input_nav goes only to the connection whose hello client name is 'hinteros-osk' (not to the launcher). osk_visibility follows if the visibility changed. Showing it again does nothing. The user can also summon it with the controller (Guide + Y by default, or A on a focused text field in a keyboard-profile Firefox app), and B hides it whatever has focus (the keyboard client never receives back while visible).

visible.description: Whether the on-screen keyboard is now visible.

password.description: (0.10) The keyboard is up for a password field (see osk_visibility). Absent when false.

error.message: the on-screen keyboard is disabled ([osk] enable = false)

osk.hide.description: Restores the previous input routing: InputPlumber's mode for whatever has focus, input_nav to the launcher while it has focus. osk_visibility follows if the visibility changed. Home and focus changes also hide it.

visible.description: Whether the on-screen keyboard is now visible.

password.description: (0.10) The keyboard is up for a password field (see osk_visibility). Absent when false.

keys.type.summary: Type text into the focused app (never into the on-screen keyboard).
keys.type.description: Characters on the US keyboard layout are typed through the daemon's virtual keyboard (uinput, with Shift for capitals and symbols; newline = Enter, tab = Tab); others go through gamescope's input method, one character at a time. Returns at once; typing happens in the background in order with other keys.* calls. Characters neither path can type are skipped and listed in 'untypeable'.

untypeable.description: Characters that were skipped, in order (duplicates kept).

error.message: no virtual keyboard (/dev/uinput) and no gamescope input method

keys.key.summary: Press and release one key, optionally with modifiers, in the focused app.
keys.key.description: For keys that are not text (function keys, shortcuts such as ctrl+l). Needs the virtual keyboard (uinput). Returns at once; the key is sent in order with other keys.* calls.

keys.action.summary: An editing action in the focused app: backspace, enter, cursor movement, ...
keys.action.description: Sent as the matching key through the virtual keyboard; without it, backspace, delete, enter and the arrows fall back to gamescope's input method. Returns at once.

system.info.summary: Relayed to the system service's system.info. What is running: release, channel, base, locked revision, generation, hostname, dev build, SSH state and host key fingerprints. Read-only.

version.description: HinterOS release of the running generation, or 'unknown'.

channel.description: Channel /etc/hinteros follows; null without a locked channel (the dev box).

dev.description: A dev build (hinteros.dev.enable): the launcher shows a DEV badge.

host_key_fingerprints.description: SHA256 fingerprints of the SSH host keys, for checking the first connection.

system.settings.get.summary: Relayed to the system service's settings.get. The user-settable view of state.json and its revision (a hash of the file). Read-only.

apps.description: Catalog app ids installed from the Store (state.json apps), in install order (since 0.3).

enabled.description: sshd runs; login is the admin account with its password.

system.settings.set.summary: Relayed to the system service's settings.set. Change state.json settings (job). Action org.hinteros.system.settings.
system.settings.set.description: changes is a closed, typed object: each settable state.json field is a property here (bool, enum, bounded integer), never free-form. It has no properties in 0.2 (SSH, base and channel have their own methods), so any field is invalid_params with data {field, reason: unknown_field}, and an empty changes object returns job_id null. revision must equal settings.get's, else state_conflict. The service writes state.json from its own typed state, never the caller's bytes.

system.ssh.set.summary: Relayed to the system service's ssh.set. Turn SSH (sshd) on or off (job). Action org.hinteros.system.ssh, which needs the admin password (auth_admin).
system.ssh.set.description: Login over SSH is the admin account with its password; the system repo configures sshd. polkit's default for this action is auth_admin. The service checks it with AllowUserInteraction (since 0.3): polkit asks the authentication agent registered for the calling process (the session daemon's, which shows the launcher a password prompt) and the call waits until the user answered (at most 5 minutes). Without an agent the call gets authentication_required; a cancelled or timed-out prompt also gives authentication_required, too many wrong passwords permission_denied (reason polkit). Returns job_id null if SSH already is in that state.

error.message: caller does not own the active seat0 session

system.generations.list.summary: Relayed to the system service's generations.list. System generations on disk (newest first). Read-only.

system.rebuild.summary: Relayed to the system service's rebuild. Re-apply the current /etc/hinteros (job): repair after a failed switch. Action org.hinteros.system.rebuild.

system.hardware.redetect.summary: Relayed to the system service's hardware.redetect. Regenerate facter.json with nixos-facter and apply it (job). Action org.hinteros.system.rebuild.

system.rollback.summary: Relayed to the system service's rollback. Switch to an earlier generation (default: the one before the current), then restore /etc/hinteros from its snapshot (job). Action org.hinteros.system.rollback.

system.update.check.summary: Relayed to the system service's update.check. Look for a newer signed revision of the channel (job), or, within 60 s of the last check, return that result without a job. Action org.hinteros.system.update.check.
system.update.check.description: The job lists the channel branch (git ls-remote of the URL from the running generation's channel table), fetches it into a root-owned bare repo, verifies the tip's SSH signature against the allowed signers shipped in the running generation, requires it to descend from the locked revision, and reads the highest Security: <low|medium|high|critical> trailer among the new commits. The job's result is an UpdateCheckResult; failures are job_failed, update_unreachable or update_verification_failed in job_finished.error.

system.update.apply.summary: Relayed to the system service's update.apply. Install the revision found by the last update.check (job). Action org.hinteros.system.update.apply.
system.update.apply.description: rev must equal the last verified check result's available.rev for the current channel and locked revision, else state_conflict. The job re-verifies it, locks the hinteros input to ?rev=<rev> (never re-fetching the branch) and runs the apply flow.

error.message: rev is not the last verified update

system.channel.set.summary: Relayed to the system service's channel.set. Follow another channel (job). Action org.hinteros.system.channel.
system.channel.set.description: The URL comes from the running generation's channel table, never from params. The target tip must be signed by an allowed signer. Moving from beta to stable, or to a tip that does not descend from the locked revision, needs acknowledge_downgrade: true (else needs_acknowledgement: at once for beta to stable, in job_finished.error for a non-fast-forward tip). Returns job_id null if the channel is already the current one.

error.message: switching from beta to stable is a downgrade

system.base.set.summary: Relayed to the system service's base.set. Switch the nixpkgs base (job). Action org.hinteros.system.channel. unstable to stable needs acknowledge_downgrade: true.

error.message: unstable to stable is a downgrade

system.apps.install.summary: Relayed to the system service's apps.install. Install Store apps (job). Action org.hinteros.system.apps.
system.apps.install.description: ids (1 to 8 catalog ids) must be in the running generation's catalog index (/run/current-system/sw/share/hinteros/catalog.json, never the caller's copy) with status available; their depends are added (transitively). Ids already installed are skipped; if nothing is left the result is job_id null. A conflict between a new app and an installed or requested one is app_conflict. Every new app with vendor terms needs accepted_terms[id] equal to the catalog's terms.version, else terms_required (the box records the acceptance: id, version, time, uid and profile, in the audit log and /var/lib/hinteros/terms-accepted.json). revision must be settings.get's (state_conflict otherwise). Free disk space must cover the new apps' sizeMiB plus the usual rebuild margin (insufficient_resources). The job writes state.json's apps from the service's typed state and runs the apply flow.

accepted_terms.description: App id to the terms version the user accepted (after reading the full text).

error.message: nope is not in this system's catalog

system.apps.remove.summary: Relayed to the system service's apps.remove. Remove installed Store apps (job), optionally with their data. Action org.hinteros.system.apps.
system.apps.remove.description: ids (1 to 8) must be installed (not_found otherwise). An app that another installed app depends on cannot be removed alone (app_conflict, conflicts_with names the dependent). The job writes state.json without them and runs the apply flow. With delete_data, after a successful switch the job deletes each removed app's dataPaths (from the running generation's catalog) in every profile's home, as root without following symlinks (each path component is opened with O_NOFOLLOW relative to the home; nothing outside the home and no other filesystem is touched) and logs what it deleted. The launcher closes running apps first.

system.jobs.get.summary: Relayed to the system service's jobs.get. One job: running or among the last 10 finished. Read-only.

system.jobs.list.summary: Relayed to the system service's jobs.list. The running job, if any, and the last 10 finished jobs, newest first. Read-only.

system.jobs.cancel.summary: Relayed to the system service's jobs.cancel. Cancel a running job before its activation stage; the box stays unchanged. Action org.hinteros.system.jobs.cancel.

error.message: the job is activating and can no longer be cancelled

network.status.summary: Wired and Wi-Fi state, the SSID joined and the IP address.
network.status.description: Runtime settings (NetworkManager over D-Bus, as the session user). The same object comes with every network_changed event.

data.reason: org.freedesktop.NetworkManager has no owner on the system bus

wifi.scan.summary: Ask for a fresh scan and return the networks it finds.
wifi.scan.description: Returns when the scan has finished (at most a few seconds); NetworkManager refuses scans right after another one, in which case the current list comes back. wifi_list_changed follows.

wifi.list.summary: The networks NetworkManager knows now, strongest first (no scan).

wifi.connect.summary: Join a network, creating a system-wide connection for it.
wifi.connect.description: The password is needed unless the network is open or already known; it is stored in NetworkManager's system connection (readable by the session user, as accepted in the threat model) and is never logged by the daemon. Returns when the connection is up (or has failed, at most about 45 s). A failed new connection is removed again. 802.1X (enterprise) networks are refused with invalid_params.

password.description: 8 to 63 characters (WPA), or 64 hex digits (the raw key).

error.message: the password for Home was not accepted
no network named Gone in range

wifi.disconnect.summary: Leave the current Wi-Fi network (it will not rejoin until connected again).

wifi.forget.summary: Delete the stored connections of a network.
wifi.forget.description: Disconnects if it is the network in use. Forgetting a network that is not stored is not an error.

bluetooth.status.summary: Whether there is an adapter, whether it is on and whether it is scanning.
bluetooth.status.description: Runtime settings (BlueZ over D-Bus, as the session user).

data.reason: org.bluez has no owner on the system bus

bluetooth.scan.summary: Start or stop looking for devices.
bluetooth.scan.description: Discovery stops by itself after timeout_s (default 30, at most 300). Found devices arrive as bluetooth_changed. While scanning (and while a bluetooth.pair is running) the daemon's pairing agent answers pairing requests; at other times it refuses them.

bluetooth.devices.summary: Known and discovered devices: paired ones first, then by name.
bluetooth.devices.description: Devices BlueZ has seen but that never reported a name are left out.

bluetooth.pair.summary: Pair with a device, trust it so that it reconnects by itself, and connect.
bluetooth.pair.description: The daemon registers a BlueZ agent (DisplayYesNo): devices without input or output (controllers, most headsets) pair without a prompt. If the device asks for a numeric comparison the daemon sends bluetooth_confirm {mode: confirm} and waits up to 30 s for bluetooth.confirm; devices that show a passkey to be typed on them get bluetooth_confirm {mode: display}. Legacy PIN requests are answered with 0000. Gives up after 45 s. Pairing an already paired device just trusts and connects it. Returns the device.

error.message: no pairing of AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:03 waits for confirmation

bluetooth.forget.summary: Unpair a device and remove it.

audio.outputs.summary: Audio outputs, which one is the default, and its volume and mute state.
audio.outputs.description: Runtime settings through PipeWire's PulseAudio interface (pactl). Every audio.* method returns this same state. An output is a sink; its id is the sink's name, stable across restarts.

audio.set_output.summary: Make an output the default: sound goes there.

audio.volume.summary: Set the default output's volume (0 to 100 percent, never above), or just report it.

audio.mute.summary: Mute or unmute the default output.

display.modes.summary: The display's modes (resolution and refresh rate), and the one in use.
display.modes.description: Under gamescope. The list is gamescope's own (the .modes file next to GAMESCOPE_PATCHED_EDID_FILE); the current mode comes from its Xwayland root window. can_set says whether display.set_mode can work (gamescope's mode save file is configured and the display is external). See the README for how modes are changed at runtime.

display.set_mode.summary: Change the display's resolution and refresh rate, until reverted or kept.
display.set_mode.description: The mode must be in display.modes. gamescope has no runtime mode request, so the daemon records the mode in gamescope's mode save file (GAMESCOPE_MODE_SAVE_FILE, keyed by the display's name) and nudges gamescope to pick the display's mode again (GAMESCOPE_DISPLAY_MODE_NUDGE). That also makes it the mode used at the next start. Returns once gamescope runs the new mode (about a second); if it does not switch, the old mode is restored and device_failed {reason: not_applied} is returned. The previous mode is remembered for display.revert. A launcher's keep-or-revert dialog calls display.keep when the user keeps it and display.revert when the time runs out.

error.message: gamescope did not switch to 1280x720@60 (is it started with -W/-H/-r?)

display.keep.summary: Accept the mode set by display.set_mode: there is nothing to revert to any more.

display.revert.summary: Go back to the mode from before the last display.set_mode (unless kept).

power.capabilities.summary: What logind says about suspend, reboot and power off for this user.
power.capabilities.description: Power goes from the session daemon straight to logind (system-api.md, Power), authorised by the polkit rules for the active local session user.

data.reason: org.freedesktop.login1 has no owner on the system bus

power.suspend.description: Returns once logind accepted the request. A system job (update, rebuild) holds a block inhibitor while it switches over: logind then refuses and the error is power_inhibited with its own text.

error.message: Operation inhibited by "hinteros-system" (PID 812), reason is "switching to a new system".

auth.respond.summary: Answer an authentication_requested prompt with the password. Only the launcher (hello client name hinteros-launcher) may call it.
auth.respond.description: The daemon runs polkit's agent helper (polkit-agent-helper-1, or polkit's helper socket) for the request's first identity with this password; the helper checks it with PAM and tells polkit. ok true: polkit authorizes the action, and the call that needed it (for example system.ssh.set) goes on; authentication_finished {outcome: authorized} follows. ok false: wrong password; the prompt stays open while attempts_left > 0 (3 tries), then the request fails (authentication_finished {outcome: failed}) and the waiting call gets permission_denied. The password is only passed to the helper: never logged, never stored, wiped from the daemon's memory after use. At most 511 bytes, no newline or NUL (invalid_params).

error.message: only the launcher answers authentication requests

auth.cancel.summary: Dismiss an authentication_requested prompt. Only the launcher may call it.
auth.cancel.description: polkit then refuses the action; the waiting call gets authentication_required. authentication_finished {outcome: cancelled} follows.

session.restart.summary: Restart the TV session: the compositor, the launcher and everything started in it, and the session daemon itself.
session.restart.description: For job_finished {session_restart_required: true} (and system_unavailable {reason: version_mismatch}). The daemon answers first, then asks logind to terminate the user's graphical session on seat0 (a greetd session: greetd's default_session starts it again at once, with the new generation's programs), then asks the user's systemd to restart the session daemon's own unit. Apps the daemon started end with it. Only a session started by greetd is ever terminated (never a desktop session). unavailable {service: logind}: no such session, or logind cannot be reached.

error.message: the graphical session was not started by greetd

store.list.summary: The App Store: the running generation's catalog, merged with what is installed.
store.list.description: From the catalog index of the running generation (/run/current-system/sw/share/hinteros/catalog.json) and system.settings.get's installed apps. Lists available apps and installed ones whatever their catalog status (retired: still works, can be removed; removed: the next update takes it away), sorted by name; apps being installed or removed through this daemon have state installing/removing. Terms carry the full text's path on this box, so the launcher can show it offline before system.apps.install. more_after_update: the last update check found apps that the next update makes installable. unavailable {service: catalog}: no index, or an index version this daemon does not read.

apps.name: Moonlight
apps.summary: Stream games from your gaming PC to the TV.
apps.description: Moonlight plays games streamed from a PC running Sunshine.

apps.name: Steam
apps.summary: Play your Steam library on the TV.

error.message: no catalog index on this system

profile.current.summary: The profile this session belongs to (the daemon's own user).
profile.current.description: setup_required: the account is a spare in first-boot mode (no admin profile exists); the launcher runs its first-boot wizard, which ends with system.profiles.setup_admin. pin_set false: a profile migrated from a single-user box without a PIN yet; the launcher asks for one before Home (system.profiles.set_pin without current_pin). screen_locked: the sleep lock is up right now (lock_state follows every change). The guest has guest true, no PIN and is never locked or admin.

name.description: Null for a spare account in first-boot mode.

locked.description: The profile asks for its PIN to enter (at the picker and after sleep).

session.switch_profile.summary: Switch to another profile (or the guest): close everything running here, then end this session; the greeter takes over.
session.switch_profile.description: The daemon calls system.profiles.switch {id} (writes the switch hint), brings the launcher to the front, sends SIGTERM to every running app (switch_progress closing_apps), asks Steam to exit (closing_steam). Nothing is force-closed silently: an app still running after switch.wait_s (10 s; Steam 15 s) produces switch_blocked and waits for session.switch_wait, session.switch_force_close or session.switch_cancel. Then it hides the keyboard, resets InputPlumber and ends its logind session (switch_progress ending). The reply comes when the switch has started, before anything closes. invalid_params {reason: same} for the session's own profile; not_found for an unknown profile; job_busy while a switch is already under way.

session.switch_wait.summary: The not-responding pop-up's Keep waiting: wait another switch.wait_s for the blocked app (switch_blocked again if it is still running).

session.switch_force_close.summary: The not-responding pop-up's Force close: SIGKILL the app's process group; the switch continues.

error.message: steam is not blocking the switch

session.switch_cancel.summary: The not-responding pop-up's Cancel switch: the profile stays (with whatever already closed gone); the hint is withdrawn.

session.unlock.summary: The sleep lock screen's PIN: relays system.profiles.unlock {pin} (the profile's own PIN, same backoff). lock_state {locked: false} follows.
session.unlock.description: A wrong PIN or an active backoff is pin_required {pin: self, retry_after_ms?}. Without a lock up: invalid_params {reason: not_locked}.

session.end_guest.summary: End guest session: guest only. Ends the session like a switch (to the picker) and wipes the guest now (home emptied, app link back to the starter set), as a reboot would.

error.message: only the guest session can be ended this way

greeter.list.summary: Greeter mode only: the picker's view of the box (/run/hinteros/profiles-public.json).
greeter.list.description: focus: the profile to focus first (the switch target, else the last used). appearance: the most accessible combination of the profiles' mirrored appearance. job: a profile job the picker should show (a removal that ended this session), else null. Only the hinteros-launcher connection may call greeter.* (not_authorized); a daemon not in greeter mode answers unavailable {service: greeter}.

error.message: this daemon is not in greeter mode

greeter.login.summary: Greeter mode only: start entering a profile (greetd create_session).
greeter.login.description: An unlocked profile, the guest or a holder of a one-time token (a just-created profile) starts at once: greeter_result {ok: true}, and the greeter session ends. A locked profile gets greeter_prompt {kind: pin}; answer with greeter.pin. Another login in progress is cancelled first.

greeter.pin.summary: Greeter mode only: the PIN for the greeter_prompt of the login in progress. The PIN goes to greetd and is wiped; greeter_result follows.

greeter.cancel.summary: Greeter mode only: give up the login in progress (greetd cancel_session). Nothing in progress is not an error.

greeter.create.summary: Greeter mode only: Add profile from the picker (profiles.create over greeter.sock, a job of about a minute). When the job succeeds, greeter.login {id} enters the new profile without its PIN (one-time token).

system.profiles.list.summary: Relayed to the system service's profiles.list. The profiles of this box, the guest and the limit. Read-only; starts a usage scan when the numbers are older than an hour.

system.profiles.create.summary: Relayed to the system service's profiles.create. Add a profile (job profiles_create: a rebuild that adds the account, about a minute). Action org.hinteros.system.profiles.create.
system.profiles.create.description: revision must be settings.get's (state_conflict otherwise). At 8 profiles: profile_limit. On success the profile has its metadata, PIN and lock flag, and its apps are the starter set; profiles_changed follows.

system.profiles.setup_admin.summary: Relayed to the system service's profiles.setup_admin. First-boot mode: make the caller's spare account the admin profile (metadata, PIN, apps = the starter set). No job, no rebuild, no network.
system.profiles.setup_admin.description: Only a spare caller, only while no admin profile exists (permission_denied otherwise).

system.profiles.rename.summary: Relayed to the system service's profiles.rename. Own profile: no PIN. Another profile: the admin PIN (pin_required {pin: admin} without it or when wrong).

system.profiles.set_appearance.summary: Relayed to the system service's profiles.set_appearance. Own profile's colour and the appearance mirrored for the picker.

system.profiles.set_pin.summary: Relayed to the system service's profiles.set_pin. Change the own PIN with the current one (current_pin left out only while no PIN is set: the migration's first PIN).

system.profiles.set_locked.summary: Relayed to the system service's profiles.set_locked. Own profile's lock flag, with the own PIN.

error.message: too many wrong PINs, try again later

system.profiles.reset_pin.summary: Relayed to the system service's profiles.reset_pin. Give another profile a new PIN with the admin PIN; for the admin profile itself no admin_pin, but the admin account's password (polkit org.hinteros.system.profiles.recover, the agent prompt).

system.profiles.remove.summary: Relayed to the system service's profiles.remove. Remove a profile with everything in it (job profiles_remove). Own PIN for the own profile (the session then ends, as in a switch), the admin PIN for another. Never the admin profile (invalid_params {reason: admin}).

error.message: the admin profile cannot be removed

system.guest.set.summary: Relayed to the system service's guest.set. Guest on or off (job guest_set, a rebuild), with the admin PIN.

system.apps.list.summary: Relayed to the system service's apps.list. The caller's own apps (its current app env's manifest). Read-only.
system.apps.list.description: revision stands for the caller's current app generation: pass it as system.apps.install and system.apps.remove's revision. needs_terms: apps that came with the starter set whose vendor terms this profile has not accepted yet (ask on first launch, system.apps.accept_terms). On a box not migrated to per-profile apps: unavailable {service: apps, reason: schema1} (then settings.get's revision and apps apply).

box.description: Box features the caller's apps need.

error.message: this box still has box-wide apps

system.apps.generations.summary: Relayed to the system service's apps.generations. The caller's app generations (current plus up to 3 earlier), newest first. Read-only.

system.apps.rollback.summary: Relayed to the system service's apps.rollback. Put the caller's apps back to an earlier generation (job apps_rollback; the box stage first if it needs a box feature that is off).

system.apps.accept_terms.summary: Relayed to the system service's apps.accept_terms. Accept the vendor terms of an app in needs_terms (first launch of a starter-set app). version must be the running catalog's terms version. Recorded by this profile.

system.starter_set.get.summary: Relayed to the system service's starter_set.get. The apps every new profile and guest session starts with. Read-only.

system.starter_set.set.summary: Relayed to the system service's starter_set.set. Change the starter set (job starter_set) with the admin PIN; ids must be among the admin profile's current apps (invalid_params {reason: not_in_admin_profile}). Affects only profiles and guest sessions created afterwards.

home_pressed.summary: The global Home button was pressed. The launcher brings itself to the front.
home_pressed.description: Sent to subscribers whichever app has focus. The daemon brings the launcher to the front itself (and sends focus_changed if focus moved); this event lets the launcher reset to its Home screen.

app_started.summary: An app was started through apps.launch.

app_exited.summary: A running app ended. If it had focus, the launcher is back in front (see focus_changed).
app_exited.description: A 'command' app has exited when its process and everything it started have exited. A Steam game has exited when its windows are gone.

exit_code.description: Exit status of the app's main process, if known (128 + signal number if it was killed).

focus_changed.summary: Another app, or the launcher (null), now has focus.

input_nav.summary: A controller navigation intent, sent to the launcher while it has focus, or only to the on-screen keyboard while it is visible.
input_nav.description: Directions repeat while held (phase 'repeat', key repeat done by the daemon; one repeating direction at a time, a new direction or a release ends it at once, events are sent immediately and never queued); other actions only press and release. While the on-screen keyboard is visible, back is not sent: B hides the keyboard. Recipients (0.4): while the on-screen keyboard is visible, only connections whose hello client name is 'hinteros-osk'; otherwise, while the launcher has focus, every other subscribed connection. Apps get the pad itself (InputPlumber PASS) or, with a keyboard input profile, key presses from the daemon; no input_nav is sent then. The launcher should map arrow keys, Enter and Escape to the same intents so it works without a controller. Clients must ignore unknown actions.

games_changed.summary: The Steam library changed (a game was installed, removed or updated, or its artwork arrived). Call games.list again.
games_changed.description: Debounced; sent only when the games.list result actually changed. Found by watching Steam's library directories (inotify), with a periodic rescan as a fallback.

apps_changed.summary: The apps.list result changed: an app's resolved icon became available or changed (for example a web app's icon finished downloading), or (0.9) the daemon reloaded its app list after a switch installed or removed apps. Call apps.list again.
apps_changed.description: Sent only when the apps.list result actually changed. Since 0.9 the daemon also reloads its app list (the generated session.toml) when it changes on disk or an apps job finished, so newly installed apps appear without a restart; apps that are running and were removed keep running until they exit. The daemon resolves icons at runtime from the box (desktop files and icon themes) or fetches and caches them (web apps), never from files it ships; fetching happens in the background after startup, so apps.list may first return apps without an icon.

steam_attention.summary: The list of Steam windows waiting to be seen changed (see steam.attention). An empty list means nothing needs attention any more.
steam_attention.description: Sent when one of Steam's own windows (Steam Guard, an update prompt, a cloud-save conflict, sign-in, ...) appears while the launcher or another app has focus, and again when such windows close or are seen. The launcher can offer 'Steam needs your attention' with an action that calls steam.focus.

osk_visibility.summary: The on-screen keyboard was shown or hidden (osk.show/osk.hide, the controller chord, A on a focused text field, B while it is visible, Home, or a focus change).
osk_visibility.description: (0.10) password is true while the keyboard is up for a password field (reported by the Firefox extension or Firefox itself in a keyboard-profile app); the keyboard should mask what it shows of the typed text then, and show it plainly otherwise (also when nothing reported a field, e.g. the keyboard was opened with the controller chord). While visible, the event is sent again (visible true) when another field of the other kind gets focus; a field losing focus changes nothing.

password.description: The keyboard is up for a password field. Absent when false.

job_started.summary: Relayed from the system service. A job was started (by any caller).

job_progress.summary: Relayed from the system service. A job reached a stage or made progress (at most 4 per second). percent only where meaningful (downloading).

job_finished.summary: Relayed from the system service. A job ended. session_restart_required: the switch replaced the system service's API or the session daemon, so the launcher should offer a session restart.

error.message: the channel tip is not signed

network_changed.summary: The network status changed (cable, Wi-Fi joined or lost, address, Wi-Fi switched).
network_changed.description: Params are what network.status returns. Debounced.

wifi_list_changed.summary: The list of Wi-Fi networks in range changed (a scan finished, a network came or went, saved networks changed).
wifi_list_changed.description: Params are what wifi.list returns. Signal changes below 5 points do not count; debounced.

bluetooth_changed.summary: The adapter's state or a device changed (found, paired, connected, battery, gone).
bluetooth_changed.description: status is what bluetooth.status returns, devices what bluetooth.devices returns. Debounced.

bluetooth_confirm.summary: A device being paired wants the user to compare or read a passkey.
bluetooth_confirm.description: mode confirm: show the passkey and answer with bluetooth.confirm {address, accept}; the daemon rejects after 30 s. mode display: show the passkey so the user can type it on the device; no answer.

audio_changed.summary: The outputs, the default output, the volume or the mute state changed.
audio_changed.description: Params are what audio.outputs returns. Debounced.

authentication_requested.summary: polkit needs the admin password for an action the launcher asked for (for example system.ssh.set): show the password dialog. Sent only to the launcher (hello client name hinteros-launcher).
authentication_requested.description: The session daemon is polkit's authentication agent for its own process, so this only happens for calls the daemon relays. Answer with auth.respond {cookie, password} (retry while attempts_left > 0) or auth.cancel {cookie}; the request is cancelled after 2 minutes without an answer. identities: whose password polkit accepts (the admin account); the daemon authenticates as the first. authentication_finished tells when the request is over.

params.message: Authentication is required to turn remote login (SSH) on or off

authentication_finished.summary: An authentication request is over: authorized, failed (too many wrong passwords) or cancelled (auth.cancel, polkit, or 2 minutes without an answer). Sent only to the launcher.

store_changed.summary: What store.list returns may have changed: an apps job started or finished, any other job that switched the system finished, or an update check changed more_after_update, or (0.9) a catalog app's icon was resolved (icon.path). Query store.list again.

switch_progress.summary: A profile switch (session.switch_profile) moved on: closing_apps (app: the one being closed, when known), closing_steam, ending (the session ends next). The launcher shows the Switching screen.

switch_blocked.summary: An app (or Steam, or a game) has not closed waited_s seconds into a switch. The launcher, in front, asks: Keep waiting (session.switch_wait), Force close (session.switch_force_close) or Cancel switch (session.switch_cancel).

lock_state.summary: The sleep lock of a locked profile: locked true before the box sleeps (the launcher is in front, apps keep running behind it; show the PIN pad on resume), false after session.unlock.

profiles_changed.summary: The profiles changed: after a profile job, a rename, a PIN, lock or appearance change. profiles is what system.profiles.list's profiles would say now (also for profile.current's fields).

greeter_prompt.summary: Greeter mode only: greetd asks something for the login in progress. kind pin: show the PIN pad (answer with greeter.pin). info and error carry greetd's message.

greeter_result.summary: Greeter mode only: the login in progress ended. ok: the profile's session starts and the greeter exits. Not ok: a wrong PIN, or locked_seconds while the backoff lock lasts (show 'Try again in N seconds'); greetd's session was cancelled, a new greeter.login starts over.

parse_error.summary: The line is not valid JSON.

invalid_request.summary: Valid JSON but not a valid JSON-RPC 2.0 request (batches are not supported).

method_not_found.summary: Unknown method (or not available in the negotiated version).

invalid_params.summary: Params do not match the method's params schema (unknown fields included), or fail a semantic check. data names the field when known.

handshake_required.summary: A method other than 'hello' was called before the handshake.

version_mismatch.summary: Client and server API versions are incompatible.

already_handshaken.summary: 'hello' was called twice on one connection.

app_not_found.summary: No such app (apps.launch: not in apps.list; apps.focus, apps.close: not running).

app_launch_failed.summary: The app could not be started (spawn failed, or it has nothing to launch).

steam_no_windows.summary: steam.focus: Steam has no windows that could be shown (not running, or no gamescope).

keyboard_unavailable.summary: keys.*: nothing can deliver the input (no virtual keyboard because /dev/uinput could not be opened, and, for text and some actions, no gamescope input method).

osk_unavailable.summary: osk.show: the on-screen keyboard is disabled in the daemon's config.

permission_denied.summary: Not allowed: the caller does not own seat0's active session (seat), polkit said no (polkit), or the peer cannot be identified safely (peer: no SO_PEERPIDFD, or the process is gone).

job_failed.summary: Only in job_finished.error and jobs.get: the job failed (or was cancelled) at stage; log_hint is the last relevant log line.

insufficient_resources.summary: Not enough memory or free disk space for a rebuild.

job_busy.summary: Another job runs (only one at a time), or the job is past the point of cancelling.

rate_limited.summary: Too many mutating requests from this user (10 per minute, burst 3).

state_conflict.summary: Stale settings revision, or update.apply's rev is not the last verified check result.

update_unreachable.summary: The update server cannot be reached (the 'home lab unreachable' screen).

update_verification_failed.summary: The channel tip is unsigned, signed by an unknown signer, or does not descend from the locked revision.

not_found.summary: Unknown generation or job; for runtime settings: a Wi-Fi network not in range, a Bluetooth device, an audio output or a display mode that does not exist, or a bluetooth.confirm with nothing waiting; system.apps.install: an id not in the running generation's catalog; system.apps.remove: an id that is not installed; auth.respond, auth.cancel: no such authentication request (or it is over).

needs_acknowledgement.summary: A downgrading channel or base switch without acknowledge_downgrade: true.

authentication_required.summary: polkit would allow the action only after interactive authentication (auth_admin: the admin password), and it did not happen: no authentication agent is registered for the caller (no session daemon agent, or another client than the session daemon called), or the user cancelled the prompt or did not answer in time.

app_conflict.summary: apps.install: id conflicts with conflicts_with (installed or also requested). apps.remove: conflicts_with, which stays installed, depends on id.

terms_required.summary: apps.install: app id has vendor terms and accepted_terms does not name their current version (show the terms, then retry with it).

system_unavailable.summary: A relayed method could not reach the system service: it is down (reason down) or speaks another system API version (reason version_mismatch, e.g. after a switch until the session restarts). The session API keeps working.

unavailable.summary: A runtime-settings method needs a service that is not there (not installed, not running, no permission to reach it, or no such hardware). Also store.list without a readable catalog index (service catalog), session.restart without a greetd session on seat0 (service logind), and auth.respond when polkit's agent helper cannot be run (service polkit).

device_failed.summary: The service accepted the request but the operation failed (a connection or pairing attempt, a mode change). The message says why in words; reason is for code.

wrong_password.summary: wifi.connect: the network refused the password.

not_authorized.summary: The service's polkit policy refused the session user (not the active local session, or the system's polkit rules are missing); auth.respond and auth.cancel from a client other than the launcher.

power_inhibited.summary: logind refused suspend, reboot or power off because an inhibitor lock blocks it (a system job is switching over). The message is logind's.

profile_limit.summary: profiles.create (greeter.create): the box has the most profiles it can have (the guest does not count).

pin_required.summary: A method needs a PIN that is missing or wrong: self (the caller's), admin (the admin profile's) or target (the profile being entered). retry_after_ms while the profile's backoff lock is active (3 free failures, then 1 s doubling up to 5 min).

Peer.description: Name and build version of one side of the connection (informational, for logs).

AppId.description: App identifier: an apps.list id, or for running apps started by command or Steam URL 'cmd-<n>' / 'steam-<appid>'. 'steam' is Steam itself (Big Picture and its other windows).

FocusTarget.description: A running app's id, or null for the launcher.

AppSource.description: How a running app was started: 'command' (an argv under the daemon's reaper), 'steam' (a Steam game), 'steam_client' (Steam's own windows: Big Picture, dialogs). Clients must treat unknown values like 'command'.

gamescope_app_id.description: The app id gamescope knows its windows by (the Steam app id for Steam games, 769 for Steam itself). For diagnostics.

pid.description: Process the daemon started for it, if it tracks one.

ExitReason.description: Why an app ended: 'exited' normally (status 0, or a Steam game's windows closed), 'crashed' (non-zero status or killed), 'launch_timeout' (a Steam game never showed a window), 'closed' (ended after apps.close, however it ended). Clients must treat unknown values like 'exited'.

NavAction.description: Navigation intent. Gamepad mapping: d-pad and left stick = directions, A/Cross = accept, B/Circle = back, Y/Triangle = context, X/Square = secondary, Start = menu, Select/View = view, L1/R1 = page_left/page_right, L2/R2 = trigger_left/trigger_right, Quick Access = quick, keyboard button = keyboard.

AppKind.description: How the app is launched. Clients must treat unknown values like 'native'.

icon.description: Absolute path to a local icon image file (PNG, SVG, ICO, JPEG, WebP), if any. Resolved by the daemon at runtime: an explicit path from the config, else the icon the app's .desktop file names, found in the installed icon themes, else (web apps) a cached download of the site's own icon. It may appear later (see apps_changed) or change. Absent: draw a placeholder, e.g. the first letter of the name.

InstallState.description: A game's install state, from its manifest's StateFlags: 'installed' (ready), 'update_required' (installed; Steam updates it before it starts, launching works), 'updating' (installed; an update is downloading or being applied), 'installing' (not fully installed yet: first download in progress or paused), 'uninstalling'. Clients must treat unknown values like 'updating' (installed, but maybe not launchable right now).

ArtworkPath.description: Absolute path of an image file in Steam's library cache (readable by the session user), or null if Steam has not cached it.

GameArtwork.description: Steam's library artwork: 'portrait' (2:3 capsule, 300x450 or 600x900), 'header' (460x215), 'hero' (wide background, e.g. 1920x620), 'logo' (transparent PNG to draw over the hero), 'icon' (small square, e.g. 32x32).

appid.description: Steam app id. Launch with apps.launch {url: 'steam://rungameid/<appid>'}; it then runs as 'steam-<appid>'.

last_played.description: When it was last played (Unix time, seconds), or null if never or unknown.

Key.description: A key on the daemon's virtual keyboard (US layout). Letters and digits are the unshifted keys: add the 'shift' modifier for capitals and symbols, or use keys.type for text. back, forward, refresh and the media keys are the multimedia keys of that name.

Modifier.description: A modifier held while a key is pressed.

SteamWindow.description: One of Steam's own top-level windows on gamescope's Xwayland.

window.description: X window id (diagnostics; stable while the window exists).

title.description: Window title as Steam set it (may be empty).

pid.description: Process that owns the window (steam or steamwebhelper), if known.

TermsVersion.description: A vendor terms version from the catalog.

AuthCookie.description: polkit's cookie for one authentication request.

StoreApp.description: A catalog entry (hinteros-catalog index version 2, fields in snake_case) with its state on this box. Removed entries (tombstones) only have id, name and status_reason; the other fields are empty.

category.description: games, video, music, photos, utilities; anything else: Other.

icon.description: Where the real icon is (HinterOS ships no logos): the installed app's desktop file, the vendor's logo URL, discovery on site_url, or the kiosk profile's favicon.

path.description: 0.9: the resolved icon on this box (absolute path to an image), when there is one: the installed app's desktop file and icon theme, or downloaded from icon_url / site_url and cached (https only; same cache, size limits and refresh as apps.list icons). Absent until resolved; store_changed is sent when it appears.

data_paths.description: Deleted in every profile's home by system.apps.remove {delete_data: true}.

terms.description: The vendor's terms, shown in full before install; null if none.

file.description: Absolute path of the plain UTF-8 text on this box.

builds_on_device.description: Fetched from the vendor and prepared on this box during install (a few minutes, needs internet).

missing_services.description: 0.12: services (box-wide, admin profile only) this app needs that are not enabled on this box. Absent or empty: none. While any is missing the app cannot be installed: say which service, and that the admin profile can install it in the Server section.

JobRef.description: A started job, or null when there was nothing to do.

rev.description: System repo revision in its config snapshot, if any.

profiles.description: 0.12: the accounts in that generation's state.json (null: unknown, e.g. no config snapshot). The rollback screen names the profiles a rollback would remove and those that would come back with an empty home.

security.description: Highest Security: trailer severity among the new commits; non-null means the launcher shows the full-screen security notice.

new_apps.description: Apps the update makes installable (in the target's catalog, not available in the running one), by id; null if the target's catalog could not be read (since 0.3). The Store says 'More apps are available after the next update'.

removed_apps.description: Installed apps the update takes away (removed from, or missing in, the target's catalog); null if unknown (since 0.3). The update screen names them with the reason.

JobResult.description: update_check jobs: an UpdateCheckResult; jobs that change the system: an AppliedResult.

ErrorObject.description: A JSON-RPC error object (codes from this document's errors).

wifi_ssid.description: The network Wi-Fi is connected to (absent when not connected).

WifiSecurity.description: wpa is WPA or WPA2 with a passphrase, wpa3 is SAE only, enterprise (802.1X) cannot be joined with a password alone.

known.description: A connection for it is stored (no password needed).

Mode.description: A display mode: pixels, and refresh rate in whole Hz (59.94 Hz is 60).

display.description: Make and model of the display, if known.

PowerCapability.description: logind's answer: challenge needs authentication nobody can give on this box.

ProfileId.description: A profile id: p<N>, server-generated, never reused.

ProfileName.description: A display name: 1 to 32 characters, trimmed, no control or format characters. Never a username.

ProfileColor.description: The profile's colour (tile and chip). Clients must treat unknown values like teal.

ProfileUsage.description: Disk use of a profile's home (hinteros-usage.service), app store paths not included.

locked_until.description: PIN backoff lock until (Unix seconds), or null.

active.description: This profile is on screen now.

PublicProfile.description: What the picker may know of a profile (profiles-public.json).

ProfileJobRef.description: A started profile job and the id the new profile will have.

system_rev.description: The system revision the env was built against.

GenerationProfile.description: An account in a system generation's state.json, with its name when this box still knows it.
